comment: Safe change management, testing and AI evaluation are discussed, but the guidance does not present an architecture-wide clinical digital safety lifecycle for safety-critical components, interfaces and data transformations. Technical conformance can be achieved while clinically hazardous behaviour remains unrecognised, especially where changes affect downstream systems or professional workflows.

reviewer.name: Robylin Tweetie Diya, RN, MSc Health Informatics (cand.)
reviewer.organisation: Independent reviewer; UK Registered Nurse; Health Informatics Specialist; Senior Systems Specialist (personal/professional capacity)

public.text: Safe change management, testing and AI evaluation are discussed, but the guidance does not present an architecture-wide clinical digital safety lifecycle for safety-critical components, interfaces and data transformations. Technical conformance can be achieved while clinically hazardous behaviour remains unrecognised, especially where changes affect downstream systems or professional workflows.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a proportionate clinical digital safety lifecycle for safety-critical DPI-H capabilities and interfaces which are hazard identification, named clinical safety accountability, safety requirements and acceptance criteria, documented risk controls, pre-deployment testing, release approval, incident response, rollback, post-implementation monitoring and reassessment triggers when data sources, models, algorithms, interfaces, intended use or deployment context materially change.
